hook.say: This morning, the post said Anthropic rebuilt version control because agent-written code pushed git into the main bottleneck. I went back in to check the surrounding numbers.

findings.label: SPEED
findings.headline: Scion cut infra footprint by 200×
findings.detail: Anthropic says the new stack uses far less CPU and memory than its git mirroring setup.
findings.evidence: Our Scion infrastructure footprint is now 200x smaller than our previous git mirroring infrastructure
findings.say: First, Anthropic says Scion made the infrastructure much lighter, with a 200-times smaller footprint than its previous git mirroring setup.

findings.label: CHECKOUT
findings.headline: CI got a 25% CPU capacity win
findings.detail: The same post says checkouts moved from minutes to seconds for CI and research jobs.
findings.evidence: CI alone realized a 25% CPU capacity win.
findings.say: Second, the operational gain was not just faster checkouts. Anthropic says CI alone saw a 25 percent CPU capacity win.

findings.label: CONTEXT
findings.headline: Google publication cites 60–70k commits a workday
findings.detail: We could not confirm this claim on the cited Google source at check time.
findings.evidence: we’ll regularly handle 60,000 to 70,000 commits to the repository per work day
findings.say: Third, a Google publication is cited for 60 to 70 thousand commits per workday, but we could not confirm that on the cited page.

take.headline: Workflow wins before tooling does
take.say: My take: workflow still matters more than tooling here. If you use Piper or similar systems, Comment CHECK and tell me.

sources.title: Google — Software Engineering at Google, Version Control at Google

caption:
This morning’s post was about Anthropic rebuilding version control because agent-written code pushed git into the bottleneck.

200× smaller infrastructure footprint versus its previous git mirroring setup.
25% CPU capacity win in CI, with checkouts moving from minutes to seconds.
A Google publication is cited for 60–70k commits per workday in Piper, but this point was not confirmed on the cited source at check time.

My take: the lesson is still workflow first. Simple review, rollback, and operational control beat complexity that only looks impressive.

Comment CHECK and I will DM you what I find.

Sources in the first comment.
